en: The Names of the Twenty-eight Yakṣa Generals,
here are the names of the four yakṣas of the eastern direction.
these are the names of the four yakṣas of the southern direction: Saṃha (1), Upasaṃha (2), Śaṅkhila (3), and Nanda (4).
The names of the four yakṣas of the western direction are:
(1) Hala, (2) Harikeśa, (3) Pāla, and (4) Piṅgala. The names of the four yakṣas of the northern direction are: [as follows].
1. Dharana, 2. Dharanānu, 3. Uṇyupayapalu, 4. Viṣṇu: these are the names of the yakṣas of the four intermediate directions.
1. Ardha-pāda (Half-foot) 2. Bhañjana (Breaking) 3. Sattvīri (Being-power) 4. Vamavata (Turning-back) The names of the four yakṣas are:
The names of the four yakṣas of the void are:
(1) Surīya, (2) Sumo, (3) Aṅgi, and (4) Vāyū; these are briefly excerpted here according to the text of the original sūtra.
The Master said: "When chanting the liturgy at the homa altar, one may chant the names of these twenty-eight yakṣas (etc.).
Some people say that *Bhañjaka* is the correct *Vijñāna* (etc.), but this is utterly erroneous. The correct [reading] is...
Since it is absolutely impossible to say that Jñāna and Pañcika are identical,
and since the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* (or *Paramādya*) lists Pañcika separately from Vimalacitra, one must know that he is a distinct yakṣa (and so forth).
On the twentieth day of the fifth month in the fifth year of Juei (1149), at dawn,
the monk Mi-i recorded that the collation was completed.
